title: aes-192, 8 rounds: Rectangle / five-byte subkey quartet recovery [HKLP05]

target.description: Initial whitening and AES192 rounds0–7, with finalMC7omitted. Source7rrectangle includesMC6; algorithm recovers five bytes of each round7 subkey, specifically K7bytes[3,5,6,9,12] for each related key, not the192-bit master keys.

setting.key_relation: Four related secret master keys K,K*,K-prime,K-prime* form an XOR parallelogram: K XOR K*=K-prime XOR K-prime*=DeltaK*, and K XOR K-prime=K* XOR K-prime*=DeltaK-prime. In column-major master-key byte positions, DeltaK* is a at9,13 and DeltaK-prime is a at1,17; other bytes are zero, with fixed a in1,...,255. These are master-key XOR differences, not chosen round keys.
setting.key_population: General related secret-key parallelogram under the exact fixed XOR differences; no weak-key class is selected.
setting.plaintext_model: Two pools of 2^84.5 plaintext pairs, one encryption per plaintext: 2^86.5 aggregate related-key chosen plaintexts.
assumptions: The source7rrectangle and false-quartet analyses use uniformity/independence approximations; component support/DDT checks are not an independent whole-attack probability proof.
Correlated5-byte key-quartet candidate count is2^40·127·2^16≈2^63, not(2^40)^4. Unknown dependentS-box differences are enumerated, not freely chosen.
